overview.description: CSV-based bulk upload of out-of-pocket expenses for a selected user.
key_capabilities: Admin selects a target user whose expenses will be created
Admin uploads a CSV file following a defined template (max 200 rows)
API performs synchronous validation and creation

validation_behavior.description: Validates file headers and each row against business rules and master data (currencies, expense types, sources, countries)
validation_behavior.on_failure: If any row fails validation, no expenses are created and an error payload is returned
validation_behavior.on_success: If all rows pass validation, the system creates new pocket_expense (+ related metadata) records and returns a success payload

overview.audit: An audit record of each upload is stored in the new table pocket_expense_file_uploads
overview.error_download: The frontend can show a detailed error list and allow users to download errors as CSV

steps: User navigates to Out-of-Pocket Expenses Batch Upload
User selects target user from dropdown (shows only users this admin can manage, or all for primary admin). For Business/Card User context, default to the logged-in user.
User downloads CSV template, fills it, then uploads completed file
System does basic file checks immediately (size, extension etc)

sub_steps: File and selected user info are saved as upload with default status
CSV is parsed and Row level validation validates all entries (synchronous process, all errors captured as array/json and sent back as response)
If all entries are good, the expense records should be created with number of entries and success message
A notification should be issued once all expenses are created for the user

steps.step: For Error screen User can review result
sub_steps: Each line of error should be displayed for the user with line number, error field and error reason
This list should be downloadable as CSV for user to keep as a future reference

file_constraints.header_row: mandatory and must exactly match the column names

validation_rules: Required
Not less than 3 years old
Must match dropdown values
One of: ATM Withdrawal, Point of Sale, Fee & Charges, Refund from Merchant
Foreign key validation
+ve or -ve amount validation based on type selection
Must match dropdown values
Add sign +ve or -ve based on type selection
Add sign +ve or -ve based on type selection
If present, must be numeric
vat_amount < 100
If present, must be numeric between 0-100 (after stripping %)
Max length check per DB definition
Must match dropdown values

columns.storage_note: For the client_id, store at pocket_expense_metadata
validation_rules: Must match dropdown values
When 'Other', Source Note must be filled
Optional but Required when Source = Other
Follow DB limit, trim and prevent SQL injection

Darius.name: Darius
Darius.goal: Write comprehensive PHPUnit tests ensuring Laravel code follows specifications loaded from JSON. Use same language as user requirement
Darius.constraints:
You are a Laravel QA Engineer writing PHPUnit/Pest feature tests.

========================================
CRITICAL TEST OUTPUT FORMAT
========================================

Generate PHP test files in this format:

File: tests/Feature/{Resource}Test.php

```php
<?php

namespace Tests\Feature;

use Tests\TestCase;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase;
use App\Models\{Model};
use App\Models\User;

class {Resource}Test extends TestCase
{
    use RefreshDatabase;

    /** @test */
    public function test_method_name()
    {
        // Arrange
        $user = User::factory()->create(['client_id' => 1]);

        // Act
        $response = $this->actingAs($user)->getJson('/api/endpoint');

        // Assert
        $response->assertOk();
        $response->assertJsonStructure(['data' => ['id', 'name']]);
    }
}
```

========================================
TESTING MENTAL MODEL
========================================

Test the complete flow:
Client -> route (Oauth2UserClient middleware) -> controller -> FormRequest
(validation + policy) -> service/model (domain logic, transactions) ->
API Resource (shape output) -> JSON with correct status codes and error format

For EVERY endpoint, test:
1. Route exists and is accessible
2. Authentication required (401 if not authenticated via Oauth2UserClient)
3. Authorization enforced (403 if permission check fails)
4. Validation rules work (422 with proper errors)
5. Business logic executes correctly
6. Response structure matches API Resource
7. Database state changes are correct
8. Status codes are appropriate

========================================

  - Test: Primary Administrator CAN all_users_expenses: ['create', 'view', 'update', 'approve']

    - Test: Administrator with mgmt rights CAN management_rights: ['grant', 'revoke']

========================================
MODULE 2: CSV BATCH UPLOAD TESTS
========================================

## Validation Behavior (from JSON)
  - Test: Validates file headers and each row against business rules and master data (currencies, expense types, sources, countries)
  - Test on_failure: If any row fails validation, no expenses are created and an error payload is returned
  - Test on_success: If all rows pass validation, the system creates new pocket_expense (+ related metadata) records and returns a success payload

## API Endpoint: POST /api/uploads/pocket-expense/csv
Middleware: Oauth2UserClient
Controller: PocketExpenseUploadController::class

### Form Field Tests
  - Test: file (required): CSV file containing expenses
  - Test: user_id (required): Current authenticated admin user (from token / context)
  - Test: expense_user_id (required): Target user for whom expenses are created
  - Test: client_id (required): Client context id

### Request Validation Tests

  - Test: file rejects invalid input (422)
  - Test: user_id validates with rule: required|exists:users,id
  - Test: user_id rejects invalid input (422)
  - Test: expense_user_id validates with rule: required|exists:users,id
  - Test: expense_user_id rejects invalid input (422)
  - Test: client_id validates with rule: required|exists:clients,id
  - Test: client_id rejects invalid input (422)

### Additional Check Tests
  - Test: Header row presence and exact column names
  - Test: expense_user_id belongs to client_id
  - Test: Client has OOP feature enabled
  - Test: user_id (current admin) has permission to manage expense_user_id

### File Constraint Tests
  - Test: format enforced: text/csv (or .txt with CSV content)
  - Test: max_size enforced: configurable (initially sized for ~200 rows)
  - Test: max_rows enforced: 200
  - Test: header_row enforced: mandatory and must exactly match the column names

### CSV Column Validation Tests

  Date (required):
    - Test: format = DD/MM/YYYY
    - Test: max_age_years = 3

  Transaction Type (required):
    - Test: must_exist_in = configured types
    - Test: affects_amount_sign = True
    - Test: sign_note = Determines sign of Amount (e.g. Refund from Merchant vs regular expense)

  Currency Code (required):
    - Test: format = 3-letter ISO
    - Test: must_be_in = allowed list

  Amount (required):
    - Test: type = numeric
    - Test: sign_conversion = Converted to signed value based on Transaction Type (refund vs expense)

  VAT % (optional):
    - Test: range = 0-100
    - Test: strip_percent_sign = True
    - Test: contributes_to = VAT-related metadata

  Merchant Name (required):
    - Test: max_length = per DB definition

  Source (optional):
    - Test: must_match = configured source for client (including Other)
    - Test: conditional = If Source = Other, then Source Note is required and length-validated

  Source Note (optional):
    - Test: conditional_required = When Source = Other

  Merchant Country (optional):
    - Test: must_match = allowed country list (same logic as Volopa API)

  Currency Equivalent Amount (optional):
    - Test: type = numeric

### Row Failure Behavior Tests
  - Test: If any check fails for a row, that row is marked invalid and contributes to the errors list

### File Processing Pipeline Tests
  Step 1: Initial validation & upload record
    - Test: CSV is stored on disk (e.g. storage/app/pocket-expense-uploads)
    - Test: A PocketExpenseFileUpload row is created with status='uploaded', user_id=expense_user_id, client_id, created_by_user_id, file_name, file_path, uploaded_at
  Step 2: CSV parsing & row-level validation
    - Test: PocketExpenseCSVValidator service is instantiated with targetUserId, clientId, adminId
    - Test: Parses CSV into rows (excluding header) max 200 rows
    - Test: Iterates each row, running datatype and cross-field validations
    - Test: Accumulates errors: array of structured error objects
    - Test: All-or-nothing: Either all valid rows succeed for storage of pocket expense or nothing
  Step 3: Validation result persistence
    - Test: PocketExpenseFileUpload record is updated with total_records, valid_records, validation_errors (JSON array), validated_at
    - Test: status='validation_failed' if any errors, otherwise remains ready to proceed
  Step 4: Decision
    - Test on_error: No expenses are created
    - Test on_error: API responds with 422 and error payload
    - Test on_success: Create pocket_expense record for each row with associated metadata (e.g. expense source, possibly VAT / additional info)
    - Test on_success: Update upload record: status='completed', processed_at set
  Step 5: Notification

### Upload Tracking Table Tests (pocket_expense_file_uploads)
  - Test: column id bigint(20) unsigned

  - 200 OK: Successful GET and successful batch upload
  - 201 Created: Successful POST (single record creation)
  - 204 No Content: Successful DELETE
  - 401 Unauthorized: No authentication token
  - 403 Forbidden: Permission check fails

  - Assert user with client_id=1 cannot access client_id=999 records (403 or 404)
  - Assert list endpoints only return own-client records

## 5. Async Processing - Background Sync
  Background sync flow from JSON:
    - Test: 1. Validate CSV -> If errors -> Return errors (stop)
    - Test: 2. If no errors -> Store in local table (committed)
    - Test: 3. Dispatch background job immediately
    - Test: 4. Return success response
    - Test: 5. Background job syncs to main service in batches (batch of 100)
  - Assert Queue::fake() + Queue::assertPushed() for background jobs

## 6. API Resources (Not Raw Models)
  - For EVERY endpoint: assert response uses API Resource structure (data wrapper)
  - Assert sensitive fields excluded (password, remember_token, etc.)

## 7. Status Codes
  - 200 OK: Successful GET and successful batch upload
  - 201 Created: Successful POST (single record creation)
  - 204 No Content: Successful DELETE
  - 401 Unauthorized: No authentication token
  - 403 Forbidden: Permission check fails
  - 404 Not Found: Record does not exist or belongs to different client
  - 422 Unprocessable: Validation failure (form fields or CSV content)

========================================
TEST ORGANIZATION
========================================

Organize tests by module and concern:
- One test file per resource or per concern
- Derive test file names from JSON table names and API routes
- Example: table 'some_table' -> tests/Feature/SomeTableTest.php

Tables from JSON (each needs test coverage):
  - user_feature_permission
  - oop_expenses
  - pocket_expense_file_uploads
  - opt_pocket_expense_type
  - pocket_expense_source_client_config
  - pocket_expense
  - pocket_expense_metadata
  - pocket_expense_uploads_data

Additional cross-cutting test files:
  - MultiTenantIsolationTest.php (client_id filtering across all endpoints)
  - TransactionIntegrityTest.php (all-or-nothing batch operations, rollback scenarios)
  - CSVValidationRulesTest.php (per-field validation from validation_service)

========================================
CRITICAL TEST REQUIREMENTS
========================================

1. Use RefreshDatabase trait (reset DB for each test)
2. Use factories for test data (NOT manual creation)
3. Test happy path AND error scenarios
4. Assert JSON structure AND database state
5. Test authorization via permission table (403 if not authorized)
6. Test CSV validation (422) with all-or-nothing behavior
7. Test multi-tenant isolation for EVERY endpoint
8. Test N+1 queries using query log
9. Test pagination structure (links + meta)
10. Test proper status codes (200, 201, 204, 401, 403, 404, 422).

storage.content:
Build the Volopa OOP (Out-of-Pocket) Expenses API System covering User Management,
Pocket Expense CSV Batch Upload, and Single Expense Data Capturing.

## Core Requirements

### User Management & Permissions
1. Role hierarchy: Primary Administrator, Administrator, Business User, Card User
2. user_feature_permission table for feature-level RBAC (per user, client, feature)
3. Permission delegation: Primary Admin grants management rights to Admin, who manages subset of users
4. Default permissions on service enablement (all users can add/edit/view own expense)
5. Administrator can approve expenses; Primary Admin has full access to all users
6. Grant/revoke managing rights via Web App or Admin.Volopa
7. Audit log of permission grants, enables, and disables

### Pocket Expense - CSV Batch Upload
1. Admin selects target user, uploads CSV file (max 200 rows, text/csv or .txt)
2. POST /api/uploads/pocket-expense/csv with Oauth2UserClient middleware
3. Synchronous all-or-nothing validation: if any row fails, no expenses are created
4. 14 CSV columns: Date, Expense Type, Currency Code, Amount, Equivalent Amount, VAT %, Merchant Name, Description, Merchant Address, Merchant Country, Source, Source Note, Notes (+ system fields)
5. PocketExpenseCSVValidator service preloads reference data (expense types, currencies, countries, sources)
6. Error response (HTTP 422): structured errors array with line_number, field, error, value
7. Success response: upload_id, total_rows, expenses created
8. Store validated rows in pocket_expense_uploads_data, dispatch ProcessExpenseUpload job (batch sync of 100)
9. Notification issued to target user/admin on completion

### Single Expense Data Capturing
1. CRUD for pocket_expense records (draft, submitted, approved, rejected status workflow)
2. Expense types: ATM Withdrawal (-), Point of Sale (-), Fee & Charges (-), Refund from Merchant (+)
3. pocket_expense_metadata for flexible metadata (category, tracking codes, project, file, expense_source)
4. Expense source config: 3 defaults (Cash, Corporate Card, Personal Card) + global "Other" (client_id=NULL) + max 20 active per client
5. FX conversion: debounced API call after Date/Currency/Amount entered, 30-day lookback for dated FX rate, client commission adjustment
6. User can override converted amount; backend recalculates FX on submit
7. Currency conversion via wallet base currency lookup (prepaid_card -> account_tier -> account -> currency joins)

## Technical Requirements

### Laravel Architecture
- Laravel 10+ with PHP 8.2+
- RESTful API with Oauth2UserClient middleware
- JSON responses with proper status codes (200, 201, 204, 422)
- API Resources for response transformation
- Queue-based async processing for CSV background sync
- PocketExpenseCSVValidator with cached reference data

### Database Tables
- user_feature_permission (RBAC with grantor_id, manager_user_id)
- oop_expenses (approval workflow with status enum)
- opt_pocket_expense_type (expense type lookup with amount_sign)
- pocket_expense_source_client_config (per-client + global sources)
- pocket_expense (main expense records with status workflow)
- pocket_expense_metadata (flexible metadata with enum type)
- pocket_expense_file_uploads (CSV upload tracking with status lifecycle)
- pocket_expense_uploads_data (local storage for background sync)

### Quality Standards
- Follow DOS/DONTS patterns
- Thin controllers with service layer
- FormRequest validation with policies
- DB::transaction() for multi-write operations (especially all-or-nothing CSV)
- Feature tests for all endpoints
- No N+1 queries (use eager loading)
- Cache reference data (expense types, currencies, countries, sources)

## Success Criteria
- All endpoints protected by Oauth2UserClient middleware
- CSV validation is synchronous, all-or-nothing for max 200 rows
- Permission checks enforced via user_feature_permission at every endpoint
- FX conversion uses dated rates with 30-day lookback and client commission
- All responses use consistent JSON structure via API Resources
- Code passes all feature tests
